title: Patients Diagnosed With Scleroderma and Their Chewing and Swallowing Performance
off: Investigating the Relationship Between the Biopsychosocial Status of Patients Diagnosed With Scleroderma and Their Chewing and Swallowing Performance
summary:
It is recommended to focus on the physical functionality, chewing, and swallowing performance of individuals diagnosed with scleroderma. There is a need to address children and adults diagnosed with scleroderma comprehensively and to evaluate them on a biopsychosocial basis to support their disease management. The aim was to assess the biopsychosocial characteristics of both children and adults diagnosed with scleroderma and to examine their chewing and swallowing performance.

Additionally, this study aims to identify effective scales that can be used in future research to assess chewing and swallowing in individuals diagnosed with scleroderma.
elig:
For a child diagnosed with scleroderma:

Inclusion Criteria:

* Cases diagnosed with scleroderma,
* Cases aged 7-18 years will be included.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Advanced heart/lung/liver/kidney disease, neurological disease, and malignancies
* Cases that are not willing to participate in the study will be excluded.
* Having participated in a regular exercise program for the past 3 months
* Individuals who are not willing to participate in the study

For adults diagnosed with scleroderma:

Inclusion Criteria:

* Individuals diagnosed with scleroderma,
* Individuals over the age of 18 will be included.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Advanced heart/lung/liver/kidney disease, neurological disease, and malignancies
* Individuals who are not willing to participate in the study will be excluded.
* Having participated in a regular exercise program for the past 3 months
* Individuals who are not willing to participate in the study

x.titre: Mastication et déglutition chez les enfants et adultes atteints de sclérodermie
x.question: Quelles sont les performances de mastication et de déglutition des patients atteints de sclérodermie, et quelles échelles permettent de les évaluer ?
x.contexte:
La sclérodermie touche la bouche et le tube digestif haut : microstomie, rigidité cutanée péribuccale, atteinte salivaire et dysphagie. Ces troubles altèrent l'alimentation et la qualité de vie, mais sont peu évalués de façon standardisée, surtout chez l'enfant.

Les recommandations insistent sur une évaluation biopsychosociale globale, comprenant la fonction physique, la mastication et la déglutition.

Cette étude observationnelle de l'université Hacettepe (Ankara) inclura 50 enfants (7 à 18 ans) et adultes atteints de sclérodermie, systémique ou localisée, vus en consultation de rhumatologie. Elle utilise des questionnaires et des tests cliniques : PEDI-EAT-10 et T-EAT-10, tests TOMASS et TOMASS-C de mastication et de déglutition de solides, test de déglutition de 90 mL d'eau, ouverture buccale maximale, limite de dysphagie. Elle vise aussi à identifier les échelles utiles pour de futures recherches.
x.interet: L'étude décrira les troubles de mastication et de déglutition de la sclérodermie et orientera le choix d'outils d'évaluation. Elle n'a pas d'effet direct sur la prise en charge.
